title: Alphabet reduction with a space bound
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let $e:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, let $f$ map binary strings to binary strings, and let $T,S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every binary input $x$, $M$ computes the letterwise $e$-image of $f(x)$ from the letterwise $e$-image of $x$ within $T(|x|)$ steps. Suppose also that on every input word $y$ over $\Gamma$ and at every time $t$, the space used by $M$ from its initial configuration on $y$ is at most $S(|y|)$. Then there are a natural number $c$ and a finite binary-alphabet machine $M'$ with the same number of work tapes as $M$ such that $M'$ computes $f$ within $n\mapsto c(T(n)+1)$ steps and, on every binary input $x$ and at every time $t$, uses at most $c(S(|x|)+1)$ space.
hypotheses_covered: $\Gamma$ is finite and has decidable equality
An embedding of the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$
Functions $f$, $T$, and $S$ on binary strings or natural numbers, as specified
$M$ computes the embedded input-output function within the stated time bound
For every $\Gamma$-alphabet input and every time, space used is at most $S$ of the input length
